requirements.original: The first component to be found killed causes the killed operation to succeed.
requirements.canonical: With the `any from` component array notation, the first component found being killed causes the `killed` operation to succeed.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- The first component to be found killed causes the killed operation to succeed.

requirements.original: The index of the matched component can optionally be assigned to an integer variable for single-dimensional component arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional component arrays.
requirements.canonical: The index of the component matched by the `killed` operation with `any from` MAY be assigned to an integer variable for a single-dimensional component array, or to an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- The index of the matched component can optionally be assigned to an integer variable for single-dimensional component arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional component arrays.

requirements.original: a) The killed operation can be used for PTCs only.
requirements.canonical: The `killed` operation SHALL be applied to PTCs only.

ambiguity.issue: "can be used for PTCs only" is phrased as a capability but is meant as a restriction.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- a) The killed operation can be used for PTCs only.

requirements.original: b) The ObjectReference followed by the killed keyword, i.e. used for identifying a specific PTC, shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of the `killed` operation SHALL be of a component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- b) The ObjectReference followed by the killed keyword, i.e. used for identifying a specific PTC, shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.original: b) The ObjectReference followed by the killed keyword, i.e. used for identifying a specific PTC, shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of the `killed` operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- b) The ObjectReference followed by the killed keyword, i.e. used for identifying a specific PTC, shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.original: c) The ComponentArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized component array.
requirements.canonical: The ComponentArrayRef of the `killed` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized component array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- c) The ComponentArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized component array.

requirements.original: d) The variable used in the (optional) value clause for storing the final local verdict of a PTC shall be of the type verdicttype.
requirements.canonical: The variable used in the value clause of the `killed` operation for storing the final local verdict of a PTC SHALL be of type `verdicttype`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- d) The variable used in the (optional) value clause for storing the final local verdict of a PTC shall be of the type verdicttype.

requirements.original: e) The (optional) value clause for storing the final local verdict of a PTC shall not be used in combination with all component or any component.
requirements.canonical: The value clause of the `killed` operation SHALL NOT be used in combination with `all component` or `any component`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- e) The (optional) value clause for storing the final local verdict of a PTC shall not be used in combination with all component or any component.

requirements.original: f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from component array construct.
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of the `killed` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is applied to an `any from` component array construct.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from component array construct.

requirements.original: g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional component arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.
requirements.canonical: The type of the integer variable used in the index redirection SHALL allow storing the highest index of the single-dimensional component array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional component array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional component arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: The size of the integer array or record of integer type used in the index redirection SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array

ambiguity.issue: "size ... the same as the dimension" could mean the number of dimensions or the size of a dimension.
readings: The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the component array.
The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the component array.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: The element type of the integer array or record of integer used in the index redirection SHALL allow storing the highest index of all dimensions of the multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the killed operation i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the killed operation.
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `killed` operation.
requirements.condition: the variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- i) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the killed operation i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the killed operation.

requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the killed operation i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the killed operation.
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the @index clause IS NOT a repeated invocation of the `killed` operation.
requirements.condition: the variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- i) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the killed operation i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the killed operation.

requirements.original: j) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone killed statements.
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used with a stand-alone `killed` statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.8 -- j) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone killed statements.

requirements.original: The keywords any and all may be used with configuration operations as indicated in table 21.
requirements.canonical: The keywords `any` and `all` MAY be used with configuration operations as indicated in table 21.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.9 -- The keywords any and all may be used with configuration operations as indicated in table 21.

requirements.original: ObjectReference "." call "(" ( FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance ) ["," SimpleExpression ] ")" [ "->" [value Ref] [verdict Ref] ] [ catch "(" timeout ")" StatementBlock ] [ catch "(" stop ")" StatementBlock ]
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `call` "(" (FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance) ["," SimpleExpression] ")" ["->" [`value` Ref] [`verdict` Ref]] [`catch` "(" `timeout` ")" StatementBlock] [`catch` "(" `stop` ")" StatementBlock].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- ObjectReference "." call "(" ( FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance ) ["," SimpleExpression ] ")" [ "->" [value Ref] [verdict Ref] ] [ catch "(" timeout ")" StatementBlock ] [ catch "(" stop ")" StatementBlock ]

requirements.original: Similar to the start operation on test components which is not blocking, the blocking call operation implicitly uses a start operation, but waits until either the started behaviour has terminated or some timeout has occurred.
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation IS blocking and implicitly uses a `start` operation on the test component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- Similar to the start operation on test components which is not blocking, the blocking call operation implicitly uses a start operation, but waits until either the started behaviour has terminated or some timeout has occurred.

requirements.original: Similar to the start operation on test components which is not blocking, the blocking call operation implicitly uses a start operation, but waits until either the started behaviour has terminated or some timeout has occurred.
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation SHALL wait until either the started test behaviour has terminated or the timeout duration has expired.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- Similar to the start operation on test components which is not blocking, the blocking call operation implicitly uses a start operation, but waits until either the started behaviour has terminated or some timeout has occurred.

requirements.original: A timeout duration in seconds can be given explicitly in the form of a SimpleExpression as an additional parameter to the call operation.
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation MAY have a timeout duration in seconds, given as a SimpleExpression additional parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- A timeout duration in seconds can be given explicitly in the form of a SimpleExpression as an additional parameter to the call operation.

requirements.original: If no timeout duration is given, an infinite timeout duration is used.
requirements.canonical: If no timeout duration is given, the `call` operation IS executed with an infinite timeout duration.
requirements.condition: no timeout duration is given in the call operation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- If no timeout duration is given, an infinite timeout duration is used.

requirements.original: Complete execution occurs when the started function is terminated by executing a return statement or if it reaches the end of the function body.
requirements.canonical: The execution of the started test behaviour IS complete when the started function terminates by executing a `return` statement or by reaching the end of its function body.

readings: The execution of a called function is complete when it executes a `return` statement or reaches the end of its body; the execution of a called altstep is complete when the altstep terminates normally after executing one of its alternatives.
Only called functions can have a complete execution; a called altstep execution is always incomplete.
ambiguity.issue: The rule only mentions functions although the call operation also accepts altstep instances (see the example a_myFourthBehaviour); the first reading is chosen as altsteps are explicitly allowed.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- Complete execution occurs when the started function is terminated by executing a return statement or if it reaches the end of the function body.

requirements.original: If the incomplete execution occurs because the called component was stopped or killed and a catch stop clause is added to the call operation, the StatementBlock of that clause is executed before the call operation terminates.
requirements.canonical: If the execution is incomplete because the called component was stopped or killed and a `catch(stop)` clause is present, the StatementBlock of the `catch(stop)` clause SHALL be executed before the `call` operation terminates.
requirements.condition: the called component was stopped or killed and a catch stop clause is added to the call operation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- If the incomplete execution occurs because the called component was stopped or killed and a catch stop clause is added to the call operation, the StatementBlock of that clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

requirements.original: If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.
requirements.canonical: If the started test behaviour does not terminate within the given timeout duration and a `catch(timeout)` clause is present, the called component SHALL be implicitly stopped.
requirements.condition: the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timeout clause is present
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

requirements.original: If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.
requirements.canonical: If the started test behaviour does not terminate within the given timeout duration and a `catch(timeout)` clause is present, the StatementBlock of the `catch(timeout)` clause SHALL be executed before the `call` operation terminates.
requirements.condition: the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timeout clause is present
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

requirements.original: In all other cases when the execution is incomplete, the call operation ends with a test case error.
requirements.canonical: If the execution is incomplete and no matching `catch(stop)` or `catch(timeout)` clause handles it, the `call` operation SHALL end with a test case error.
requirements.condition: execution is incomplete and not handled by a catch clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- In all other cases when the execution is incomplete, the call operation ends with a test case error.

requirements.condition: the execution of the started behaviour is complete

requirements.canonical: A `call` operation MAY have a redirect clause with a `verdict` clause that assigns the termination verdict of the called component to a variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- Additionally, a redirect clause can be added to the operation which allows assignment of the return result (in case that the called function has a return clause) to a variable via the value clause and also the assignment of the termination verdict of the called component via the verdict clause.

requirements.original: In all cases of incomplete execution, the variables referenced in the value and verdict clause or in out and inout actual parameters will stay unchanged and no assignment will be made.
requirements.canonical: In all cases of incomplete execution, the variables referenced in the `value` and `verdict` clauses and in `out` and `inout` actual parameters SHALL stay unchanged and no assignment SHALL be made.
requirements.condition: the execution of the started behaviour is incomplete
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- In all cases of incomplete execution, the variables referenced in the value and verdict clause or in out and inout actual parameters will stay unchanged and no assignment will be made.

requirements.original: If the called component is not created alive and has already been started or called once or if it has been killed, additional call operations are not allowed.
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation SHALL NOT be applied to a test component that is not created alive and has already been started or called once, nor to a test component that has been killed.
requirements.condition: the called component is non-alive and has already been started or called, or it has been killed

readings: A call operation is not allowed on a killed test component (alive or not) and on a non-alive test component that has already been started or called once.
A call operation is not allowed on a non-alive test component that has already been started, called or killed; the killed condition only applies to non-alive components.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of 'or if it has been killed' is unclear; the first reading is chosen since a killed component of any kind cannot execute behaviour. The text also does not say whether violation is a compile-time or runtime error; the example shows it is a test case error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- If the called component is not created alive and has already been started or called once or if it has been killed, additional call operations are not allowed.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `call` operation SHALL be of a component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type.

requirements.original: b) The function or altstep invoked in a call test component operation shall have a runs `on definition` referencing a component type to which the called component is compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7).
requirements.canonical: The function or altstep invoked in a `call` operation SHALL have a `runs on` clause referencing a component type to which the called component is compatible.

ambiguity.issue: 'runs on definition' is used instead of the usual 'runs on clause', and 'call test component operation' instead of 'call operation'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.10 -- b) The function or altstep invoked in a call test component operation shall have a runs `on definition` referencing a component type to which the called component is compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7).
